en.title: Optimize Box IDs (Same as Amazon #34 in the Main Algorithm Library)
en.description:
Amazon MERN #5 is an interleaved algorithm problem that is already included in the main algorithm library; it is the same problem as Amazon #34 "Get Minimum String (Box Lex-Smallest)". The Amazon #13 that the #5 page points to is actually a different interval-counting problem, so this entry is mapped to #34 by its title and problem meaning.

One operation takes out any digit d, changes it to min(d+1,9), and inserts it at any position. Any number of operations (including 0) may be performed; find the lexicographically smallest final string, keeping leading zeros.

This site's standard I/O, examples, and judging reuse the verified Amazon #34 and do not redefine the operation.
en.input: A single line containing a digit string of length 1..200000.
en.output: Output the lexicographically smallest digit string, keeping leading zeros.
en.explanation: This problem is the same as Amazon #34 and reuses its verified examples, reference implementation, and tests; the original #5 link to Amazon #13 is unrelated to this problem.
hints: Scan from right to left while maintaining the minimum digit on the right. If the current digit is greater than that minimum, it must be moved and incremented by 1; the rest stay. Finally, sort the transformed digits.
